item.title: Ari Fleischer rebukes Vance: Iran ceasefire, not war, cost Republicans the election
item.description: Former White House press secretary Ari Fleischer disputes VP Vance's explanation for Republican midterm losses, arguing the US should have finished the war with Iran.

item.title: Michael Rabello will not run again for State Comptroller
item.description: Attorney Michael Rabello, who served as Prime Minister Netanyahu's personal lawyer, has withdrawn his candidacy for State Comptroller following the election results.

item.title: One dead, two injured in helicopter crash near Miami
item.description:
One person was killed and two others were injured when a helicopter crashed into the waters of Biscayne Bay near Miami, Florida. The two injured men were taken to a trauma center in serious but stable condition.
According to authorities, the three men aboard the helicopter were filming boats at the time of the crash. The cause of the accident remains under investigation.

item.title: Report: Bennett to demand Knesset Speaker position for his party
item.description:
Together party chairman Naftali Bennett intends to demand the position of Knesset Speaker, Channel 13 News reported.
According to the report, Bennett wants the position to go either to a member of his party or to another agreed-upon candidate who is not a member of Gadi Eisenkot's party.

item.description: Lebanon's Hezbollah-affiliated Al Mayadeen network reported a strike in the area between the villages of Markaba and Talloussa in southern Lebanon.

item.title: Hakeem Jeffries launches bid for House Speaker after Democrats' midterm victory
item.description: House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries formally announces his bid for speaker following his party's landslide midterm victory, with little opposition expected.

item.title: Will the Hasidic faction split? Degel HaTorah will not endorse any candidate
item.description: Following instructions from leading Lithuanian haredi rabbis, Degel HaTorah will not endorse any candidate for prime minister, while divisions may emerge within United Torah Judaism's Hasidic faction.

item.title: Wallah! The European Left begins to fear its pact with the devil
item.description: According to the report of the French parliamentary commission of inquiry, “political Islam is not a fantasy, not an extrapolation, but a real, documented and visible threat." America, are you listening? Op-ed.

item.title: Feiglin opens door to all parties: 'We do not rule anyone out'
item.description: Feiglin recommends Netanyahu to President Herzog but demands new elections over alleged foreign interference, while setting conditions for joining a coalition.

item.title: Never Before Seen: The Jerusalem Apartment Raffle Is Back With a Huge Surprise
item.description: Dreaming of a luxury apartment in Jerusalem? Am Yisrael Chai’s Dream Raffle is back and bigger than ever for its ninth year in a row. What’s new about this year’s apartment? And what exactly is the “Super Ticket"? Here’s everything you need to know.

item.title: "Broad govt, without terror supporters": Netanyahu issues first statement since elections
item.description: The Prime Minister warned against a coalition dependent on parties he described as "supporters of terrorism" and accused left-wing bloc leaders of setting conditions designed to prevent the formation of a broad government.

item.title: Feiglin asks Herzog to consider pardon for convicted Duma murderer
item.description:
Zehut party chairman Moshe Feiglin asked President Isaac Herzog to consider granting a pardon to Amiram Ben Uliel, who was convicted of murdering three members of the Dawabshe family in the village of Duma.
"In the past, as a member of the Knesset, I worked to secure the release of Roman Zadorov. I ask you to reconsider the issue of granting Amiram Ben Uliel a pardon and securing his release," Feiglin told Herzog.

item.title: Shabbat in a Changed Israel: How Israelis have embraced Shabbat since October 7
item.description: For those who are not used to keeping Shabbat, even with the right supplies, taking on Shabbat can be a formidable challenge, yet a growing number of Jews in Israel have embraced this foundational mitzvah.

item.title: Eisenkot: 'The people of Israel voted for change'
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot promises to establish a national emergency government, strengthen bipartisan support for Israel in Washington, and deepen cooperation with President Trump.

item.title: Hebron: The city of our forefathers lives again
item.description: The Jewish bond with Hebron began with Avraham's own life there, was strengthened by his purchase of the Cave of Machpelah, and became a source of faith for generations after him.

item.title: Chuck Schumer sold his soul, now his betrayal is complete
item.description: This is Chuck Schumer’s legacy, a Democratic Party that openly embraces Jew-hate, that defends terrorism and the attempted murder of Jewish children while protecting antisemites at all costs. Opinion.

item.title: Forer tells Herzog: No to Arab parties, but Likud is not disqualified
item.description: Yisrael Beytenu representative Oded Forer made clear that his party does not rule out cooperation with Likud but refuses to serve in a government alongside the Arab parties.

item.title: Trump responds to Vance's comments on Iran war: 'True, but do it again'
item.description:
Asked about Vice President JD Vance's statement attributing the Republican Party's failures in the midterm elections to the Iran war, US President Donald Trump said he believes it is "largely true because it drove the gasoline up."
That being said, he added: "At the same time, if I had to do it again, I'd have to do it again because, long-term, it's the only answer. You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon. You have no choice"
Read more.

item.title: Agudat Yisrael will not recommend any candidate to form the government
item.description:
The Agudat Yisrael faction announced that it will not endorse any candidate for prime minister during its meeting with President Isaac Herzog.
However, two party members, Meir Porush and Elyakim Stark, are considering separately recommending Benjamin Netanyahu to form the next government, but have not yet announced their final decisions.

item.title: Degel Hatorah faction will not recommend any candidate to form the government
item.description:
The Degel Hatorah faction announced that its representatives will not recommend any candidate to President Isaac Herzog to form the next government.
The decision was made at the instruction of the party's rabbinic leaders, Rabbi Dov Lando and Rabbi Moshe Hillel Hirsch.

item.title: Shin Bet chief estimates suspected foreign election interference at NIS 100 million
item.description: The head of the Shin Bet estimated that the suspected foreign interference in the elections involved NIS 100 million, Channel 12 News reported.

item.title: Oded Forer: 'Yisrael Beytenu had hoped for a more decisive election outcome'
item.description: The Yisrael Beytenu faction participated in the round of consultations with President Isaac Herzog. After recommending Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, MK Oded Forer said, "Yisrael Beytenu had hoped for a more decisive election outcome."

item.title: The Democrat's victory and the new politics of Jewish vulnerability
item.description: The critical question this election raises is whether American Jews still have a secure future in the U.S., or if domestic politics will begin to mirror the exceptional, double standards that have long been demanded of the Jewish state globally. Analysis.

item.title: Deri to resign from Knesset, remain Shas chairman
item.description:
Aryeh Deri met on Wednesday evening with Rabbi Moshe Maya, the senior member of the Shas Council of Torah Sages.
It was announced that Deri will resign from the Knesset but will continue to serve as chairman of the party.
Read more.

item.title: The goal: A broad national government led by Netanyahu
item.description: Following their meeting with President Herzog, Minister Orit Strock and incoming MKs Itamar Eitam and Tzvika Mor discussed the possibility of forming a broad national government.
